claim: Intermittent fasting (IF) has been shown to reduce cardiovascular risk factors in both animals and humans.
source: Intermittent fasting (IF) has been shown to reduce cardiovascular risk factors in both animals and humans, and can protect the heart against ischemic injury in models of myocardial infarction.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research establishing these effects.

claim: IF can protect the heart against ischemic injury in models of myocardial infarction.
source: Intermittent fasting (IF) has been shown to reduce cardiovascular risk factors in both animals and humans, and can protect the heart against ischemic injury in models of myocardial infarction.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on myocardial infarction models.

claim: The underlying molecular mechanisms behind IF's cardiovascular effects remain unclear.
source: However, the underlying molecular mechanisms behind these effects remain unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The study conducted comprehensive system-wide analyses of the proteome, phosphoproteome, and transcriptome of heart tissues from mice on different IF regimens.
source: To shed light on the molecular and cellular adaptations of the heart to IF, we conducted comprehensive system-wide analyses of the proteome, phosphoproteome, and transcriptome, followed by functional analysis.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: Heart tissues were obtained from mice maintained on daily 12- or 16 hr fasting, every-other-day fasting, or ad libitum control feeding regimens for 6 months.
source: Using advanced mass spectrometry, we profiled the proteome and phosphoproteome of heart tissues obtained from mice that were maintained on daily 12- or 16 hr fasting, every-other-day fasting, or ad libitum control feeding regimens for 6 months.
evidence: This describes the experimental design and sample collection.

claim: IF significantly affected pathways that regulate cyclic GMP signaling, lipid and amino acid metabolism, cell adhesion, cell death, and inflammation.
source: Our analyses revealed that IF significantly affected pathways that regulate cyclic GMP signaling, lipid and amino acid metabolism, cell adhesion, cell death, and inflammation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the multi-omics analyses conducted in the study.

claim: The impact of IF on different metabolic processes varied depending on the length of the fasting regimen.
source: Furthermore, we found that the impact of IF on different metabolic processes varied depending on the length of the fasting regimen.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing different IF regimens in the study.

claim: Short IF regimens showed a higher correlation of pathway alteration.
source: Short IF regimens showed a higher correlation of pathway alteration, while longer IF regimens had an inverse correlation of metabolic processes such as fatty acid oxidation and immune processes.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of different IF regimens.

claim: Longer IF regimens had an inverse correlation of metabolic processes such as fatty acid oxidation and immune processes.
source: Short IF regimens showed a higher correlation of pathway alteration, while longer IF regimens had an inverse correlation of metabolic processes such as fatty acid oxidation and immune processes.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of different IF regimens.

claim: Functional echocardiographic analyses demonstrated that IF enhances stress-induced cardiac performance.
source: Additionally, functional echocardiographic analyses demonstrated that IF enhances stress-induced cardiac performance.
evidence: This is a finding from the functional cardiac assessment experiments.

claim: In the developed world, the average calorie intake has steadily risen.
source: In the developed world, the average calorie intake has steadily risen, as have associated age-related diseases (Lahey and Khan, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Age-related diseases have risen in the developed world.
source: In the developed world, the average calorie intake has steadily risen, as have associated age-related diseases (Lahey and Khan, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Intermittent fasting eating patterns include frequent periods of 12–24 hr with little or no energy intake sufficient to trigger a metabolic switch from the utilization of liver-derived glucose to fatty acids and ketones.
source: Intermittent fasting (IF) eating patterns include frequent periods of 12–24 hr with little or no energy intake sufficient to trigger a metabolic switch from the utilization of liver-derived glucose to fatty acids and ketones.
evidence: This is a definition based on established scientific knowledge about IF.

claim: IF eating patterns increase health span and lifespan in animals.
source: Such IF eating patterns increase health span and lifespan and delay or prevent age-associated diseases in animals (de Cabo and Mattson, 2019; Mattson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: IF eating patterns delay or prevent age-associated diseases in animals.
source: Such IF eating patterns increase health span and lifespan and delay or prevent age-associated diseases in animals (de Cabo and Mattson, 2019; Mattson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Rodents maintained on IF exhibit reduced resting heart rate and blood pressure.
source: Rodents maintained on IF exhibit reduced resting heart rate and blood pressure, increased heart rate variability, and improved cardiovascular adaptations to stress (Mager et al., 2006; Wan et al., 2003a; Wan et al., 2003b; Wan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Rodents maintained on IF exhibit increased heart rate variability.
source: Rodents maintained on IF exhibit reduced resting heart rate and blood pressure, increased heart rate variability, and improved cardiovascular adaptations to stress (Mager et al., 2006; Wan et al., 2003a; Wan et al., 2003b; Wan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Rodents maintained on IF exhibit improved cardiovascular adaptations to stress.
source: Rodents maintained on IF exhibit reduced resting heart rate and blood pressure, increased heart rate variability, and improved cardiovascular adaptations to stress (Mager et al., 2006; Wan et al., 2003a; Wan et al., 2003b; Wan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Age-related increases in oxidative stress, inflammation, and fibrosis in the heart are prevented by every-other-day (EOD) fasting.
source: Age-related increases in oxidative stress, inflammation, and fibrosis in the heart are prevented by every-other-day (EOD) fasting (Castello et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: IF improves health indicators and cardiovascular risk factors in human subjects.
source: IF also improves health indicators and cardiovascular risk factors in human subjects (Harvie et al., 2011; Harvie et al., 2013; Stein et al., 2012; Weiss and Fontana, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Alternate day fasting improved cardiovascular markers in a recent randomized controlled trial.
source: In a recent randomized controlled trial, alternate day fasting improved cardiovascular markers, reduced fat mass, fat-to-lean ratio, and increased levels of the ketone β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) (Stekovic et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a specific clinical trial.

claim: Alternate day fasting reduced fat mass and fat-to-lean ratio in a recent randomized controlled trial.
source: In a recent randomized controlled trial, alternate day fasting improved cardiovascular markers, reduced fat mass, fat-to-lean ratio, and increased levels of the ketone β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) (Stekovic et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a specific clinical trial.

claim: Alternate day fasting increased levels of the ketone β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) in a recent randomized controlled trial.
source: In a recent randomized controlled trial, alternate day fasting improved cardiovascular markers, reduced fat mass, fat-to-lean ratio, and increased levels of the ketone β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) (Stekovic et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a specific clinical trial.

claim: IF protects the brain and heart against ischemic injury in animal models.
source: IF protects the brain and heart against ischemic injury and enhances endurance in animal models (Arumugam et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2018; Marosi et al., 2018; Mattson and Arumugam, 2018; Wan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: IF enhances endurance in animal models.
source: IF protects the brain and heart against ischemic injury and enhances endurance in animal models (Arumugam et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2018; Marosi et al., 2018; Mattson and Arumugam, 2018; Wan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Animals maintained on EOD fasting prior to experimental myocardial infarction (MI) have a reduced myocardial infarct size compared to ad libitum fed controls.
source: Animals maintained on EOD fasting prior to experimental myocardial infarction (MI) have a reduced myocardial infarct size compared to the ad libitum (AL) fed controls (Ahmet et al., 2011; Ahmet et al., 2005; Godar et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: IF improves survival and recovery of heart function when initiated two weeks after MI.
source: IF also improves survival and recovery of heart function when initiated two weeks after MI (Katare et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: IF engages signaling pathways that enhance cellular stress resistance, mitochondrial biogenesis, and autophagy in brain and skeletal muscle.
source: Recent brain and skeletal muscle studies suggest that IF engages signaling pathways that enhance cellular stress resistance, mitochondrial biogenesis, and autophagy (Marosi et al., 2018; Mattson and Arumugam, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The ketone BHB may mediate some cellular adaptations to fasting.
source: The ketone BHB may mediate some cellular adaptations to fasting, including inducing the expression of the inhibitory neurotransmitter γ-aminobutyric acid, trophic factors, and the cytoprotective mitochondrial deacetylase sirtuin 3 (Cheng et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2019; Marosi et al., 2016; Newman and Verdin, 2017; Yudkoff et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: It is unknown whether similar molecular and cellular mechanisms underlie the beneficial effects of IF on the cardiovascular system.
source: However, it is unknown whether similar molecular and cellular mechanisms underlie the beneficial effects of IF on the cardiovascular system.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: System-wide interrogation using large-scale omics technologies has proven powerful in capturing snapshots of molecular abundances in an unbiased manner.
source: System-wide interrogation using large-scale omics technologies has proven powerful in capturing snapshots of molecular abundances in an unbiased manner.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of omics technologies based on established knowledge.

claim: Previous studies have extensively focused on understanding the metabolic rewiring associated with different modes of fasting and feeding responses in the liver and adipose tissues.
source: Previous studies have extensively focused on understanding the metabolic rewiring associated with different modes of fasting and feeding responses in the liver, the primary metabolic and secretory organ, and adipose tissues that functions as a fat sensor (Ng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Recent technological advancements have positioned mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics as a rational choice to simultaneously track the dynamic behavior of thousands of proteins.
source: Though transcriptomics remained the go-to technology for many of the earlier works in this arena, recent technological advancements have positioned mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics as a rational choice to simultaneously track the dynamic behavior of thousands of proteins, the prime orchestrators of cellular processes, in a global manner.
evidence: This is a statement about technological advancements in the field.

claim: Protein post-translational modifications, especially phosphorylation, underlie several energy sensor pathways, glucose homeostasis mechanisms, and insulin secretion process.
source: Protein post-translational modifications, especially phosphorylation, underlie several energy sensor pathways, glucose homeostasis mechanisms, and insulin secretion process, and hence deconvolution of phosphorylation networks is key to understanding signaling alterations (Sacco et al., 2019; Sacco et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The importance of IF in improving cardiovascular health has been extensively documented.
source: While the importance of IF in improving cardiovascular health has been extensively documented, a global investigation documenting the molecular players driven by the metabolic switch would be highly desirable.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The study employed advanced mass spectrometry for system-wide profiling of the proteome and phosphoproteome of heart tissues from mice with daily fasting for 12 hr (IF12), 16 hr (IF16) or EOD as well as AL control feeding.
source: In order to understand molecular and cellular remodeling of the heart during IF, we employed advanced mass spectrometry for system-wide profiling of the proteome and phosphoproteome of heart tissues obtained from mice with daily fasting for 12 hr (IF12), 16 hr (IF16) or EOD as well as AL control feeding.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: The study performed transcriptome analyses using RNA sequencing to evaluate whether the observed molecular responses to IF occur at the transcriptional or post-transcriptional levels.
source: We also performed transcriptome analyses using RNA sequencing to evaluate whether the observed molecular responses to IF occur at the transcriptional or post-transcriptional levels.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: IF profoundly modifies pathways involved in metabolism, cell signaling, and epigenetic reprogramming in the heart.
source: Our results indicated that IF profoundly modifies pathways involved in metabolism, cell signaling, and epigenetic reprogramming in the heart.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the multi-omics analyses conducted in the study.

claim: Protein network remodeling during IF occurred in an IF duration time-dependent manner, with IF16 and EOD having the most significant effects.
source: Of note, we observed that protein network remodeling during IF occurred in an IF duration time-dependent manner, with IF16 and EOD having the most significant effects.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of different IF regimens.

claim: Functional studies indicated that IF improves cardiac function compared to AL feeding.
source: In addition, functional studies indicated that IF improves cardiac function compared to AL feeding.
evidence: This is a finding from the functional cardiac assessment experiments.

claim: All in vivo experimental procedures were approved by the National University of Singapore (Ethics approval number: R15-1568) and La Trobe University (Ethics approval number: AEC21012) Animal Care and Use Committees.
source: All in vivo experimental procedures were approved by the National University of Singapore (Ethics approval number: R15-1568) and La Trobe University (Ethics approval number: AEC21012) Animal Care and Use Committees and performed according to the guidelines set forth by the National Advisory Committee for Laboratory Animal Research (NACLAR), Singapore, and Australian Code for the Care and Use of Animals for Scientific Purposes (8th edition) and confirmed NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.
evidence: This is a statement about the ethical approval for the study.

claim: C57BL/6 male mice were purchased at 2 months of age.
source: C57BL/6 male mice were purchased at 2 months of age (InVivos, Singapore; ARC, Australia) and housed in the animal facility at the National University of Singapore and La Trobe University.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects used in the study.

claim: The animals were exposed to light from 07:00-19:00 (12 hr light: 12 hr dark cycle).
source: The animals were exposed to light from 07:00-19:00 (12 hr light: 12 hr dark cycle) and were fed with pellets for rodents which consisted of 58%, 24%, and 18% of calories originating from carbohydrate, protein, and fat, respectively (Teklad Global 18% Protein rodent diet #2918; Envigo, Madison, WI, USA).
evidence: This describes the housing conditions for the experimental animals.

claim: The animals were fed with pellets consisting of 58%, 24%, and 18% of calories originating from carbohydrate, protein, and fat, respectively.
source: The animals were exposed to light from 07:00-19:00 (12 hr light: 12 hr dark cycle) and were fed with pellets for rodents which consisted of 58%, 24%, and 18% of calories originating from carbohydrate, protein, and fat, respectively (Teklad Global 18% Protein rodent diet #2918; Envigo, Madison, WI, USA).
evidence: This describes the diet composition for the experimental animals.

claim: At the age of 3 months, the mice were randomly assigned to four different dietary intervention groups: IF12 (N=20), IF16 (N=60), EOD (N=20), and AL group as a control (N=60).
source: At the age of 3 months, the mice were randomly assigned to the four different dietary intervention groups: IF12 (N=20), IF16 (N=60), EOD (Every Other Day fasting) (N=20), and AL group as a control (N=60).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and group assignments.

claim: The mice in the IF12, IF16, and EOD groups fasted for 6 months.
source: The mice in the IF12, IF16, and EOD groups fasted for 6 months daily 12 hr (19:00-07:00), 16 hr (15:00-07:00), or 24 hr (a whole day fasting followed by an entire day feeding).
evidence: This describes the duration and timing of the fasting regimens.

claim: Mice in the EOD group exhibited a large and highly significant decrease in blood glucose levels throughout the duration of the study.
source: In contrast, mice in the EOD group exhibited a large and highly significant decrease in blood glucose levels throughout the duration of the study (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a finding from the physiological measurements conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: On fasting days, mice in the EOD group exhibited blood ketone levels that were threefold greater than mice in the AL group.
source: On fasting days, mice in the EOD group exhibited blood ketone levels that were threefold greater than mice in the AL group.
evidence: This is a finding from the physiological measurements conducted in the study.

claim: All IF and EOD animals exhibited significantly lower body weight than AL mice.
source: Notably, all IF and EOD animals exhibited significantly lower body weight than AL mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a finding from the physiological measurements conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: No significant difference in overall body weight was observed between the IF and EOD groups.
source: However, despite the differences in the fasting regimen pattern, we did not observe any difference in overall body weight between the IF and EOD groups (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a finding from the physiological measurements conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: No significant difference in the overall energy intake or compositional intake was observed across mice subjected to IF groups compared to the AL group.
source: Furthermore, no significant difference in the overall energy intake or compositional intake is observed across mice subjected to IF groups compared to the AL group (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a finding from the dietary intake measurements conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: Using tandem mass tag (TMT)-based high resolution liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis, the study identified a total of 6972 proteins.
source: Using tandem mass tag (TMT)-based high resolution liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis, we identified a total of 6972 proteins (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Among the 5578 proteins quantified across all samples, 9% were differentially expressed among the heart tissues from different dietary regimens compared to the control AL group.
source: Among the 5578 proteins quantified across all the samples, 9% of the proteins were differentially expressed among the heart tissues from different dietary regimens compared to the control AL group (Dunnett adjusted p-value = 0.01, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Only 60 proteins consistently overlapped with altered protein levels across all fasting regimens and were primarily involved in processes associated with glycogen catabolism, fatty acid oxidation, and glycolysis.
source: Among these, only 60 proteins consistently overlapped with altered protein levels across all fasting regimens and were primarily involved in processes associated with glycogen catabolism, fatty acid oxidation, and glycolysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: The EOD group exhibited the most significant number of protein abundance changes, with 44% modulations exclusively occurring within this group.
source: The EOD group exhibited the most significant number of protein abundance changes, with 44% modulations exclusively occurring within this group, including apolipoproteins that are important determinants of a healthy heart (Liehn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Approximately one-third of the differentially expressed proteins in IF groups compared to AL were enzymes with catalytic activity involved in energy homeostasis pathways.
source: Approximately one-third of the differentially expressed proteins in IF groups compared to AL were enzymes with catalytic activity involved in energy homeostasis pathways.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Most of the enzymes involved in glycolysis, including the rate-limiting enzyme phosphofructokinase (PFKFKB1/2) displayed decreased expression with IF except for hexokinase 1 (HK1).
source: We observed that most of the enzymes involved in glycolysis, including the rate-limiting enzyme phosphofructokinase (PFKFKB1/2) displayed decreased expression with IF except for hexokinase 1 (HK1), indicative of suppression of glycolysis (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: The expression of phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PCK2), which is involved in gluconeogenesis, was enhanced by IF.
source: Conversely, the expression of phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PCK2), which is involved in gluconeogenesis, was enhanced by IF.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: A distinct class of proteins showed increased abundance only in the EOD group, belonging to processes such as mRNA processing, fatty acid metabolism, autophagy, and stress response mechanisms.
source: Unlike clusters in IF16 and IF12 groups, which exhibited modest differences compared to the AL group, a distinct class of proteins showed increased abundance only in the EOD group. These clusters of proteins with exclusive upregulation in the EOD (FDR <0.05) group belonged to processes such as mRNA processing, fatty acid metabolism, autophagy, and stress response mechanisms.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Processes such as cholesterol transport and phospholipid efflux showed a downward trend in the EOD group.
source: Other processes such as cholesterol transport and phospholipid efflux showed a downward trend in the EOD group.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Several metabolic processes, including oxidative phosphorylation, amine catabolism, and fatty acid oxidation, were overall reduced in all IF groups compared to AL.
source: Several other metabolic processes, including oxidative phosphorylation, amine catabolism, and fatty acid oxidation, were overall reduced in all IF groups compared to AL.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Major determinants of insulin sensitivity such as AKT1 and mTOR were highly expressed with EOD.
source: With EOD, major determinants of insulin sensitivity such as AKT1 and mTOR were highly expressed, and several other stress-activated kinases MAPK9 and MAPK10, showed reduced abundance (Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to figures.

claim: Stress-activated kinases MAPK9 and MAPK10 showed reduced abundance with EOD.
source: With EOD, major determinants of insulin sensitivity such as AKT1 and mTOR were highly expressed, and several other stress-activated kinases MAPK9 and MAPK10, showed reduced abundance (Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to figures.

claim: Structural proteins involved in processes such as focal adhesion and cell adhesion were upregulated across all fasting regimens.
source: We observed upregulation of structural proteins involved processes such as focal adhesion and cell adhesion across all fasting regimens suggesting possible re-organization of the extracellular matrix interaction in heart tissues with IF.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Proteins regulating lipid kinase activity were observed in higher abundance in the hearts of mice from all three IF regimens compared to AL.
source: In addition, proteins regulating lipid kinase activity were observed in higher abundance in the hearts of mice from all three IF regimens compared to AL.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: The IF12 group showed enrichment of proteins associated with cyclase activity.
source: For example, the IF12 group showed enrichment of proteins associated with cyclase activity, while the IF16 group displayed elevation of ERK signaling proteins.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: The IF16 group displayed elevation of ERK signaling proteins.
source: For example, the IF12 group showed enrichment of proteins associated with cyclase activity, while the IF16 group displayed elevation of ERK signaling proteins.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Signaling pathways involving the second messenger cAMP were activated only with longer periods of fasting.
source: Signaling pathways involving the second messenger cAMP, however, were activated only with longer periods of fasting.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) metabolism was significantly lower in all IF groups compared to the AL group.
source: Apart from components of lipid metabolism and transport that were reduced across all IF groups, our data also showed that branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) metabolism, which is known to regulate several anabolic and catabolic cellular cascades (Gannon et al., 2018), was significantly lower in all IF groups compared to the AL group (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: IF12 enhanced the processes that maintain the structural integrity of the heart, such as adhesion, extracellular structure, and cytoskeletal organization.
source: Compared to AL, IF12 enhanced the processes that maintain the structural integrity of the heart, such as adhesion, extracellular structure, and cytoskeletal organization (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: IF12 increased expression of proteins involved in the immune and stress response, and endocytosis and exocytosis events.
source: We also observed increased expression of proteins involved in the immune and stress response, and endocytosis and exocytosis events in IF12.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Proteins involved in metabolic processes such as sterol metabolism and transport, glucose utilization, and protein synthesis were downregulated by IF12.
source: As expected, proteins involved in metabolic processes such as sterol metabolism and transport, glucose utilization, and protein synthesis were downregulated (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: Immune functional networks (NF-κB and Wnt signaling, innate immune response, and T cell receptor signaling) and amino acid biosynthetic processes were downregulated in IF16 in comparison with IF12.
source: While the protein trafficking network was enhanced in IF16, other immune functional networks (NF-κB and Wnt signaling, innate immune response, and T cell receptor signaling) and amino acid biosynthetic processes were downregulated in IF16 in comparison with IF12 (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: EOD led to epigenetic changes compared to IF16.
source: EOD introduced a wide spectrum of changes in the heart proteome. In addition to metabolic changes commonly, EOD led to epigenetic changes compared to IF16 (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: Proteins associated with chromatin remodeling and organization, and those involved in histone and other protein modifications showed increased abundance with EOD.
source: Proteins associated with chromatin remodeling and organization, and those involved in histone and other protein modifications showed increased abundance.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: An increase in the mitotic and nuclear division regulatory networks was observed with EOD.
source: Also, an increase in the mitotic and nuclear division regulatory networks was observed.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: EOD exhibited a reduced abundance of components involved in mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC), pyruvate metabolism, and ATP generation compared to IF16 mice.
source: Along with reduced immune response and ion and sterol transport, EOD exhibited a reduced abundance of components involved in mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC), pyruvate metabolism, and ATP generation compared to IF16 mice (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: EOD fasting downregulated blood coagulation.
source: EOD fasting also downregulated blood coagulation which may be crucial to reducing risk of pathological clot formation.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomics analysis conducted in the study.

claim: Comparison of correlation across transcripts and proteins abundance across the different groups revealed only a modest correlation (Pearson correlation coefficient ~0.47).
source: Comparison of correlation across transcripts and proteins abundance across the different groups revealed only a modest correlation as expected (Pearson correlation coefficient ~0.47; Figure 2—figure supplement 2a), ruling out any regimen-specific differences.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of transcriptome and proteome data, with reference to a figure.

claim: Structural processes such as ECM-receptor interaction and metabolic pathways involving BCAA degradation showed consistent changes in proteome and transcriptome with IF.
source: This revealed that structural processes such as ECM-receptor interaction and metabolic pathways involving BCAA degradation showed consistent changes in proteome and transcriptome with IF (Figure 2d and Figure 2—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of transcriptome and proteome data, with reference to figures.

claim: With increased fasting hours, mainly in the EOD group, a trend shift in the direction of proteome and transcriptome abundances was observed.
source: Nevertheless, with increased fasting hours, mainly in the EOD group, we observed a trend shift in the direction of proteome and transcriptome abundances (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of transcriptome and proteome data, with reference to a figure.

claim: Metabolic processes associated with fatty acid oxidation and monocarboxylic acid catabolic processes and immune processes related to autoimmunity and chemokine signaling showed the most noticeable drifts between proteome and transcriptome.
source: Metabolic processes associated with fatty acid oxidation and monocarboxylic acid catabolic processes and immune processes related to autoimmunity and chemokine signaling showed the most noticeable drifts.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of transcriptome and proteome data.

claim: Many of the key enzymes involved in the beta-oxidation of unsaturated (ECI1/2) and long-chain (or very long-chain) fatty acids (HADHA/B and ACADVL) showed differential transcript and protein abundances.
source: On investigating the fatty acid oxidation cluster, we noticed that many of the key enzymes involved in the beta-oxidation of unsaturated (ECI1/2) and long-chain (or very long-chain) fatty acids (HADHA/B and ACADVL) showed differential transcript and protein abundances suggesting plausible buffering of protein levels beyond transcriptional regulation with IF.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of transcriptome and proteome data.

claim: Phospholipid phosphatase 1 (PLPP1) showed a dramatic decrease in protein abundance in the EOD group despite a modest increase in the corresponding transcript abundance.
source: Phospholipid phosphatase 1 (PLPP1) which is involved in the synthesis of glycerolipids and lipid uptake showed a dramatic decrease in protein abundance in the EOD group despite a modest increase in the corresponding transcript abundance.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of transcriptome and proteome data.

claim: N-acetyltransferase NAT10, ribonuclease RNASE4, and spliceosome-associated protein CWC27 all showed an exclusive increase only in the protein level with no observed changes in the mRNA level.
source: N-acetyltransferase NAT10 involved in histone acetylation and chromatin organization, ribonuclease RNASE4 participating in mRNA cleavage, and spliceosome-associated protein CWC27 involved in mRNA splicing all showed an exclusive increase only in the protein level with no observed changes in the mRNA level.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of transcriptome and proteome data.

claim: Both the IF12 and IF16 groups were similar to the EOD fasting group in terms of clock gene transcript expression despite the time-restricted feeding during daytime.
source: Notably, both the IF12 and IF16 groups were similar to the EOD fasting group despite the time-restricted feeding during daytime.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptome analysis of clock genes.

claim: Changes in around 79 proteins appeared early within the IF12 regimen and some of these alterations were conserved until longer fasting durations at both IF16 and EOD.
source: Changes in around 79 proteins appeared early within the IF12 regimen and some of these alterations were conserved until longer fasting durations at both IF16 and EOD (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis.

claim: Highly populated network clusters exclusively emerged with EOD that contributed to 189 proteins in the overall IF-modulated network.
source: Highly populated network clusters exclusively emerged with EOD that contributed to 189 proteins in the overall IF-modulated network (Figure 3a), suggesting enhanced network rewiring with longer fasting duration.
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The cluster that constituted proteins associated with fatty acid beta-oxidation and PPAR was the most highly enriched cluster.
source: The cluster that constituted proteins associated with fatty acid beta-oxidation and PPAR was the most highly enriched cluster exemplifying the impact of IF on lipid oxidation.
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis.

claim: Many of the proteins associated with the fatty acid beta-oxidation and PPAR cluster tend to be downregulated during IF, particularly in EOD, except for a few proteins such as ACOT1, ACOT2, and EHHADH that showed high abundances exclusively with EOD.
source: It was evident that many of the proteins associated with this cluster tend to be downregulated during IF, particularly in EOD, except for a few proteins such as ACOT1, ACOT2, and EHHADH that showed high abundances exclusively with EOD (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Cardioprotective roles have been attributed to the fatty acyl-CoA thioesterase ACOT1 via its activation of PPARα/PGC1α signaling.
source: Indeed, cardioprotective roles have been attributed to the fatty acyl-CoA thioesterase ACOT1 via its activation of PPARα/PGC1α signaling (Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The most prominent effects of IF on lipid metabolism were on the apolipoproteins APOA1/4, APOE, and APOC1/2/3, all of which declined in the EOD group.
source: The most prominent effects of IF on lipid metabolism were on the apolipoproteins APOA1/4, APOE, and APOC1/2/3, all of which declined in the EOD group.
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis.

claim: An increase in the level of NPC2, an intracellular transporter mediating the export of cholesterol from lysosomes, was observed in the EOD group.
source: An increase in the level of NPC2, an intracellular transporter mediating the export of cholesterol from lysosomes (Pfeffer, 2019), was observed in the EOD group.
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis.

claim: PLTP, the increased activity of which is known to be associated with atherosclerosis, systolic dysfunction, obesity, and diabetes, was observed to be suppressed explicitly in all three IF groups.
source: PLTP, the increased activity of which is known to be associated with atherosclerosis, systolic dysfunction, obesity, and diabetes (Chowaniec and Skoczyńska, 2018), was observed to be suppressed explicitly in all three IF groups.
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis.

claim: Signal transduction primarily via the insulin receptor and MAPK pathways emerged as one of the prominent clusters primarily comprising proteins modulated with longer fasting duration.
source: Apart from these lipid-linked clusters, we also observed other clusters differentially modulated in an IF group-dependent manner. Signal transduction primarily via the insulin receptor and MAPK pathways emerged as one of the prominent clusters primarily comprising proteins modulated with longer fasting duration (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: B2M, a risk marker for cardiovascular disease, was found within the signal transduction cluster.
source: B2M, a risk marker for cardiovascular disease (Shi et al., 2021), was found within this cluster.
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis.

claim: LNPEP, a zinc-dependent aminopeptidase that cleaves several peptide hormones and also catalyzes the conversion of angiotensinogen to cardioprotective angiotensin IV (AT4), was upregulated by IF16.
source: Upregulated by IF16 within this cluster was LNPEP, a zinc-dependent aminopeptidase that cleaves several peptide hormones and also catalyzes the conversion of angiotensinogen to cardioprotective angiotensin IV (AT4) (Stragier et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from the protein-protein interaction network analysis.

claim: Several key transcription factors with metabolic relevance including PPARα/γ, FOXA1/2, NUCKS1, HNF4A were found to be enriched.
source: Several key transcription factors with metabolic relevance including PPARα/γ, FOXA1/2, NUCKS1, HNF4A among others were found to be enriched.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcription factor enrichment analysis.

claim: The correlation network comprised 44,966 associating protein pairs, of which a majority (34,629 pairs) involved positive co-regulations between the associated proteins.
source: The correlation network comprised 44,966 associating protein pairs, of which a majority (34,629 pairs) involved positive co-regulations between the associated proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 7a-b).
evidence: This is a finding from the protein co-regulation network analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Higher deviations by ~40% across all IF groups than the AL group were observed, suggestive of dynamic modulation of protein associations with IF.
source: This revealed higher deviations by ~40% across all IF groups than the AL group, suggestive of dynamic modulation of protein associations with IF.
evidence: This is a finding from the protein co-regulation network analysis.

claim: The greatest number of affected proteins in the perturbation association network was identified in the IF16 and EOD groups, with the EOD group showing exclusive changes in 118 proteins and the IF16 group with 69 altered proteins.
source: We identified consensus proteins that were consistently altered in protein associations across the different IF regimens (P-value <0.05) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 7c) and accordingly identified the greatest number of affected proteins in the IF16 and EOD groups, with the EOD group showing exclusive changes in 118 proteins and the IF16 group with 69 altered proteins.
evidence: This is a finding from the perturbation association network analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Most of the perturbed proteins involved in metabolic pathways were also localized to the mitochondria.
source: A consistent pattern across the inferred association perturbations was that most of these involved proteins in the metabolic pathways were also localized to the mitochondria (Figure 3—figure supplement 4a).
evidence: This is a finding from the perturbation association network analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Among the 12,540 phosphorylated sites identified on 2931 proteins, ~80% and ~19% sites were phosphorylated on serine and threonine respectively, with only 1% being tyrosine phosphorylated.
source: Among the different groups, we identified 12,540 phosphorylated sites on 2931 proteins of which, ~80% and~19% sites were phosphorylated on serine and threonine respectively, with only 1% being tyrosine phosphorylated.
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis.

claim: Peptides with single phosphorylation sites represented 81% of the phosphopeptides analyzed.
source: Peptides with single phosphorylation sites represented 81% of the phosphopeptides analyzed.
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis.

claim: 66% of the identified phosphorylation sites corresponded with those curated in the PhosphoSitePlus database.
source: Among the sites identified, 66% corresponded with those curated in the PhosphoSitePlus database (Hornbeck et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis.

claim: Phosphorylation changes varied with increasing duration of the fasting period with EOD exhibiting the greatest number of phosphosite abundance changes.
source: On assessing those sites that were significantly altered (Dunnett adjusted p-value <0.05) with IF, we observed that phosphorylation changes varied with increasing duration of the fasting period with EOD exhibiting the greatest number of phosphosite abundance changes, similar to what was observed in the proteome (Figure 4a and Supplementary file 8b).
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Phosphoproteome profiling revealed increased phosphosite abundance on a majority of the differentially modulated phosphoproteins, and several of these were independent of proteome changes.
source: However, in contrast to proteome remodeling, phosphoproteome profiling revealed increased phosphosite abundance on a majority of the differentially modulated phosphoproteins, and several of these were independent of proteome changes.
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis.

claim: Site-specific phosphorylation changes occurred on several proteins involved in structural remodeling of the heart, such as titin.
source: Site-specific phosphorylation changes occurred on several proteins involved in structural remodeling of the heart, such as titin, which was observed with multiple changes (Figure 4a), and on regulatory proteins, including kinases, phosphatases, and enzymes in metabolic pathways (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: PKA/PKC were commonly activated across all IF regimens based on kinase motif enrichment analysis.
source: PKA/PKC were commonly activated across all IF regimens.
evidence: This is a finding from the kinase motif enrichment analysis of phosphoproteomics data.

claim: CSNK and p38 signaling were exclusive to the IF16 group based on kinase motif enrichment analysis.
source: CSNK and p38 signaling were exclusive to the IF16 group, while AMPK, the master regulator of energy metabolism, exhibited activation in longer fasting groups.
evidence: This is a finding from the kinase motif enrichment analysis of phosphoproteomics data.

claim: AMPK exhibited activation in longer fasting groups based on kinase motif enrichment analysis.
source: CSNK and p38 signaling were exclusive to the IF16 group, while AMPK, the master regulator of energy metabolism, exhibited activation in longer fasting groups.
evidence: This is a finding from the kinase motif enrichment analysis of phosphoproteomics data.

claim: Pathways associated with insulin signaling, focal adhesion, and cGMP-PKG signaling were conserved across all IF groups based on phosphoproteome analysis.
source: Pathway-based assessment of the modulated phosphoproteins highlighted the conserved modulation of pathways associated with insulin signaling, focal adhesion, and cGMP-PKG signaling across all IF groups (Figure 4c–d).
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: cGMP-PKG signaling is known to mediate vasorelaxation, and activation of this pathway is regarded as cardioprotective.
source: cGMP-PKG signaling is known to mediate vasorelaxation, and activation of this pathway is regarded as cardioprotective (Kukreja et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Components of AMPK signaling showed significant modulation in both IF16 and EOD groups based on phosphoproteome analysis.
source: In line with the kinase prediction, components of AMPK signaling showed significant modulation in both IF16 and EOD groups (Figure 4c–d).
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: Expression levels of pAMPK/AMPK, PPARγ, MYPT1, and IRS1 were significantly higher in the IF16 group compared to the AL group based on immunoblot validation.
source: In line with our proteomic inferences, compared to the AL group, expression levels of pAMPK/AMPK, PPARγ, MYPT1, and IRS1 were significantly higher in the IF16 group.
evidence: This is a finding from the immunoblot validation experiments.

claim: The increase in heart rate, as well as ejection fraction, fractional shortening and left ventricular dimensions after dobutamine stress were significantly higher in IF16 mice compared with AL control mice.
source: However, the increase in heart rate, as well as ejection fraction, fractional shortening and left ventricular dimensions after stress were significantly higher in IF16 mice compared with AL control mice (Supplementary file 9, Figure 6a, Figure 6—videos 1–4), suggesting that IF preserves myocardial functional reserve.
evidence: This is a finding from the echocardiographic analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Longitudinal and radial strain significantly improved after dobutamine administration in IF16 mice but not in AL mice.
source: Longitudinal and radial strain significantly improved after dobutamine administration in IF16 mice but not in AL mice, suggesting that IF preserved systolic contractile reserve, which deteriorated with age in the AL mice (Supplementary file 9, Figure 6b).
evidence: This is a finding from the echocardiographic strain analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: IF preserved systolic contractile reserve, which deteriorated with age in the AL mice.
source: Longitudinal and radial strain significantly improved after dobutamine administration in IF16 mice but not in AL mice, suggesting that IF preserved systolic contractile reserve, which deteriorated with age in the AL mice (Supplementary file 9, Figure 6b).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the echocardiographic strain analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Both IF and regular exercise training increase parasympathetic tone and heart rate variability.
source: For example, both IF and regular exercise training increase parasympathetic tone and heart rate variability, and both can protect the myocardium against ischemic injury (Rengo et al., 2013; Voulgari et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Both IF and regular exercise training can protect the myocardium against ischemic injury.
source: For example, both IF and regular exercise training increase parasympathetic tone and heart rate variability, and both can protect the myocardium against ischemic injury (Rengo et al., 2013; Voulgari et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Both exercise and IF stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis in skeletal muscle.
source: Moreover, both exercise and IF stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis in skeletal muscle (Marosi et al., 2018; Drake et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Exercise training stimulates mitochondrial biogenesis in myocardial cells.
source: Exercise training also stimulates mitochondrial biogenesis in myocardial cells (Bernardo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: IF activates several major pathways engaged by ischemic and metabolic preconditioning, including upregulation of protein chaperones, anti-apoptotic proteins, and autophagy, and suppression of the mTOR pathway and protein synthesis in brain and skeletal muscle.
source: Studies of the effects of IF on the brain and skeletal muscle suggest that IF activates several major pathways engaged by ischemic and metabolic preconditioning, including upregulation of protein chaperones, anti-apoptotic proteins, and autophagy, and suppression of the mTOR pathway and protein synthesis (Marosi et al., 2018; Mattson and Arumugam, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: ACOT1 functions as a molecular rheostat to impede excessive fatty acid oxidation during fasting and dampens associated inflammation and oxidative stress by inducing protective PPARα signaling.
source: ACOT1, for instance, functions as a molecular rheostat to impede excessive fatty acid oxidation during fasting and dampens associated inflammation and oxidative stress by inducing protective PPARα signaling (Franklin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: PKA is one of the key modulators of PPAR transcriptional activity, especially in the context of lipid oxidation during fasting and exercise.
source: It is noteworthy that signaling alterations driving such PPAR-associated modulations were also evident from IF-induced phosphorylation changes, including activation of PKA, one of the key modulators of PPAR transcriptional activity, especially in the context of lipid oxidation during fasting and exercise (Lazennec et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: PKA triggers glycogen breakdown by activating phosphorylase kinase PHKB, which in turn triggers glycogen phosphorylase to release glucose 1 phosphate from glycogen.
source: In addition to modulating fatty acid flux, PKA also triggers glycogen breakdown by activating phosphorylase kinase PHKB, which in turn triggers glycogen phosphorylase to release glucose 1 phosphate from glycogen (Brushia and Walsh, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The cAMP/PKA axis plays crucial modulatory roles in various aspects of cardiac physiology, including cardiomyocyte contractility via excitation–contraction coupling (ECC), control of heart rate, and downstream relay of β-adrenergic receptor signaling.
source: The cAMP/PKA axis plays crucial modulatory roles in various aspects of cardiac physiology, including cardiomyocyte contractility via excitation–contraction coupling (ECC), control of heart rate, and downstream relay of β-adrenergic receptor signaling, is known to be perturbed in instances of heart failure (Bockus and Humphries, 2015; Callaghan, 2016; Lissandron and Zaccolo, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Disruption of GLUT4 trafficking is associated with impaired glucose uptake and ensuing insulin resistance.
source: Disruption of GLUT4 trafficking is associated with impaired glucose uptake and ensuing insulin resistance (Mueckler, 2001), and the phosphorylation change on TBC1D1 and GLUT4 along with the predicted increase in AKT activity suggest that IF improves insulin sensitivity in the heart by modulating glucose uptake and resetting aberrations in insulin signaling via increasing phosphorylation of such proteins.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Titin is a crucial determinant of myocardial passive stiffness and whose malfunction is associated with various myopathies.
source: In addition, there was a striking increase in phosphorylation of epitopes on numerous proteins known to regulate heart development and cardiomyocyte contraction, particularly that is a crucial determinant of myocardial passive stiffness and whose malfunction is associated with various myopathies (LeWinter and Granzier, 2014; Makarenko et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cardiomyocytes account for only 30% of cells in the mammalian heart and yet account for the majority of the cardiac mass.
source: Such a limitation is exaggerated, particularly for the transcriptome analysis, as cardiomyocytes account for only 30% of cells in the mammalian heart and yet account for the majority of the cardiac mass (Zhou and Pu, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Time-restricted feeding/intermittent fasting cycles impact and can reset secondary tissue-specific peripheral clocks independent of the master circadian clock that is generally phase-locked to light-dark cycles.
source: It has been established that time-restricted feeding/intermittent fasting cycles impact and can reset secondary tissue-specific peripheral clocks independent of the master circadian clock that is generally phase-locked to light-dark cycles (Damiola et al., 2000; Hara et al., 2001; Stokkan et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Previous studies established that the EOD regimen leads to hearts with thinner walls and a lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV).
source: It is noteworthy that previous studies established that the EOD regimen leads to hearts with thinner walls and a lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (Ahmet et al., 2005) and lower blood pressure and heart rate (Wan et al., 2003a) than those of control animals.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The EOD regimen leads to lower blood pressure and heart rate than those of control animals.
source: It is noteworthy that previous studies established that the EOD regimen leads to hearts with thinner walls and a lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (Ahmet et al., 2005) and lower blood pressure and heart rate (Wan et al., 2003a) than those of control animals.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The effects of EOD were associated with cardioprotection in a rat model of myocardial infarction.
source: The latter effects of EOD were associated with cardioprotection in a rat model of myocardial infarction (Ahmet et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.
